reconciliation_result.required_before_any_retry: a monotonic version/tombstone/generation or equivalent authoritative fence proving that the prior canonical effect cannot have existed and then been deleted/replaced behind the checkpoint

observations: An authoritative-looking absence is not by itself sufficient to distinguish never-committed from committed-then-deleted/replaced or a stale/non-monotonic read after acknowledgement loss.
Without a history-preserving fence, retrying create on E could duplicate or resurrect an effect, so the fixture suppresses both create and overwrite.

The safe recurring-Chat checkpoint therefore needs more than stable effect identity and payload hash for this branch: it must preserve a transport-provided monotonic version/tombstone/generation fence, or else retain the outcome as unresolved and defer mutation.
inference: Within this exact deterministic model, idempotency by stable effect identity plus payload hash is insufficient after acknowledgement loss when the later lookup returns absence and the transport exposes no monotonic history fence. Safe resumption requires treating absence as ambiguous and forbidding mutation retry. This does not prove that any concrete allowed repository/API transport supplies or lacks such fencing, and it makes no liveness claim under indefinite ambiguity.
